commits_sample.message:
fix: recover partial check data when a check suite App is not viewable by the token

The v12 prechecks GraphQL queries request checkSuite { app { databaseId } }
for every check run. When the workflow token cannot view the GitHub App that
owns a check suite (for example, the Actions GITHUB_TOKEN reading check runs
created by another App installed on the repository), GitHub returns per-node
FORBIDDEN errors alongside an otherwise valid response, and octokit throws
away the usable partial data - failing every deployment on such repositories.

Recover the partial response when every reported error is that App access
failure. The nulled App identity is already handled as an optional
disambiguation hint by latestCheckResults.
commits_sample.author: Alec Hartung

notes: Feature identification uses both source branches and pull requests.
Historical PRs are retained even when their source branch no longer exists.
Deployment correlation uses deployment ref/SHA and normalized DEV/TEST/PROD environment names.
Only data returned by the GitHub API is treated as evidence; missing stages remain null.
The GitHub helper functions currently request up to 100 items per endpoint/page.
A missing DEV/TEST/PROD timestamp means the available GitHub evidence could not reliably correlate that stage to the feature; it does not prove that no deployment occurred elsewhere.
